### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a5b05ced1ca5671c89bbea303d112b327af20468` — the merge of head `1bd1ba175673e6f4d194a556fb71b0ae23b1c051` into base `5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a5b05ced1ca5671c89bbea303d112b327af20468 && git checkout a5b05ced1ca5671c89bbea303d112b327af20468
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812 1bd1ba175673e6f4d194a556fb71b0ae23b1c051 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812 && git merge --no-ff 1bd1ba175673e6f4d194a556fb71b0ae23b1c051

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5656c5638abfcee5081571e6c7c5f5c8998a1812` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1bd1ba175673e6f4d194a556fb71b0ae23b1c051`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23225 (body and all 13 comments, the D2b claim `6160651537` as amended, the `os-dev-report` `6162772892`, the ACCEPT `6162852069`); PR #23411's body, its 16-file list and the net diff against the merge base `e4ec6ec1a` (+1218 / -14); ADR-0138 at `origin/main` (D2, D2b, the four axes, the enforcement map, the unsettled items, the E2 row); the 47 check-runs on the head. Committed source was read with `git show` / `git grep` against the two fetched refs only. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The eight new `@objectstack/spec/api` exports — right.** Five functions (`anonymousFlowDoorTarget`, `anonymousElevatedFlowPairs`, `anonymousEndpointElevatedFlowMessage`, `elevatedFlowAnonymousEndpointsMessage`, `validateAnonymousElevatedFlows`) and three interfaces (`AnonymousFlowDoorCandidate`, `ElevatedFlowCandidate`, `AnonymousElevatedFlowPair`), all declared in `endpoint-publish-gate.ts` section (f) and re-exported by `src/api/index.ts`; `api-surface/api.json` and `export-origins/api.json` each gain exactly those eight, each origin pointing at that file. They exist because the record puts the cross-item read "beside `policyGate`" in spec while two doors outside spec (`MetadataManager.publishPackage`, the metadata protocol's flow publish) must call the same judge: one judge, three doors, no second implementation (PD #12). The judge is pure and total: `anonymousFlowDoorTarget` reads `type === 'flow'`, `authRequired === false` exactly (an absent key is the schema default `true`, so never anonymous) and a non-empty string `target`; `anonymousElevatedFlowPairs` indexes flows with `runAs === 'system'` by name and pairs in endpoint order; a flow with an absent `runAs` reads as the default `user`. The pinned edges in `anonymous-elevated-flow-gate.test.ts` (an `object_operation` endpoint sharing the flow's name, an absent `authRequired`, a `system` flow of another name, an unnamed endpoint reported as `apis[i]`) match the code. This is a public-surface widening and is declared as one (②).

**The stack-schema refinement — right, and every embedder inherits it.** `applyApiEndpointGates` now takes `flows` and runs `validateAnonymousElevatedFlows(config.apis, config.flows)` before the per-endpoint `validateApiEndpointDeclarations` loop, raising one `custom` issue per pair at `['apis', i, 'authRequired']` with the endpoint-direction sentence. Because `superRefine` reads the parsed output, the schema defaults have already applied, so the judge's exact-value reads are sound at this door. Both items are in the one input, so the stack is refused whichever was edited last, which is the record's "both directions" at this door; the spec test pins each direction as the edit that completes the pair from an accepted stack (the two accepted stacks are the negative controls), plus `defineStack` raising `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 with the issue located. A pair is reported beside, not instead of, a missing armed budget (ADR-0121 D6), so D2b is not a cascade of D6: right, a pair is a fact about two declarations. Embedders: `ObjectStackSchema` is the same lazy schema (`stack.zod.ts:1888`) and `EnvironmentArtifactSchema.metadata` embeds `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` itself (`system/environment-artifact.zod.ts:132`), so the artifact load, `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build`, the lint scorer and the metadata plugin's artifact ingestion (`plugin.ts:1321`) all run the leg with no copy to drift. `ArtifactPackageSchema.manifest` is `AssembledPackageBodySchema`, which never carried the endpoint gates, so a per-package artifact entry is judged exactly as before; a pair whose two halves sit in two packages of one composition is outside the stack door's reach, the same scope the per-endpoint gates have always had, and the PR's acceptance notes say so.

**The composition with `applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate` — unchanged and unreordered.** At the head, `stack.zod.ts:1853` reads `}).superRefine(applyApiEndpointGates).superRefine(applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate));`, byte-identical to `origin/main:1833`. The diff touches `applyApiEndpointGates`'s body and signature only; the D2b leg runs inside it, before the per-endpoint gates; the owner-binding gate still runs second. `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal`, `assertLockAllowsDelete` and `restoreArtifactRegistryView` are not in the diff.

**`MetadataManager.publishPackage`'s new refusal — right, both directions.** `gateAnonymousElevatedFlowsForPublish` runs right after `gateApiItemsForPublish`, outside the `shouldValidate` branch (a security refusal with an opt-out flag is no refusal; `validate: false` is pinned not to disable it). It reads both types through `listForIndex` (the registry and every loader, rethrowing a loader failure, so a publish fails instead of answering "nothing names it" from a read that did not happen), peels the stored envelope as `gateApiItemsForPublish` and `buildEndpointIndex` do, and reports: an `api` item of the package naming a `system` flow anywhere in the index at the endpoint (a pair inside the package once, at the endpoint); a `flow` item of the package declaring `system` that an anonymous endpoint outside the package names at the flow. The errors ride the existing `validationErrors` / `success: false` result, nothing is published (pinned: `itemsPublished 0`, state stays `draft`), and each message is the direction's sentence with the prescription. `packageNamesOf` keeps both the registry key and the body's `name`, so a disagreement cannot hide an item from its own package.

**The metadata protocol's flow-publish refusal — right, and the one-direction shape is right.** `anonymousElevatedFlowRefusal` judges `flow` items declaring `runAs: 'system'` only, reads the engine registry's `api` items and the `metadata` service's `list('api')` (the two sources `getMetaItems` reads), hands them to the one judge with `[{ name, runAs: 'system' }]`, and throws `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 with `issues[0].path: 'runAs'`, the envelope that door's other publish-time contract refusals carry; the error's `message` is the flow-direction sentence with the prescription, the per-key issue carries the reason and the endpoint names. It is asked at every door a flow body reaches `active` through: `saveMetaItem` when `mode !== 'draft' && writeSource !== 'migrate-stored'`, placed after the schema parse and before the authoring gate and every write (beside the default-record-page refusal); and `promoteDraftForPublish` on `draftForGate.body` before `repo.promoteDraft`, which `publishMetaItem` (`protocol.ts:23676`) and `publishPackageDrafts` (`:25061`) share, so a batch aborts on it (pinned, with the draft kept). Only the flow direction sits here, and that is right: `api` is `allowRuntimeCreate: false` (`metadata-plugin.zod.ts:1130`) and the protocol's code-only inlet refuses its write, so no endpoint is ever published through this door; the endpoint direction lives at the two doors that publish endpoints (the stack parse and the package publish). The saves it deliberately does not judge: a draft save (a draft does not execute, and its promotion is judged, both pinned in section 5) and a `migrate-stored` re-save (it rewrites a row that already exists, and the credential move exists to take a secret out of that row). The `migrate-stored` skip is not a wire bypass: `source` is stated only by `migrateStoredMetadata`, and `rest-server.ts` builds the save request field by field without a client-supplied `source`. A row that already pairs keeps executing as published until its next publish, which the semantic entry's acceptance criteria say to an upgrading author.

**Both directions at every door the diff names, each refusal with the prescription — yes.** Stack parse: both, as one input. Package publish: both, at the package's own item. Protocol: the flow direction, the only direction that door can hold. The record's prescription, "an authenticated endpoint for a partner that can hold a credential; the signed inbound-hook channel (ADR-0041) for a partner webhook; a public form for anonymous intake", is carried verbatim in substance by both sentences (`ANONYMOUS_ELEVATED_FLOW_PRESCRIPTION`), the prescription before the reason so a truncated 4xx keeps it. `runAs: 'automation'` is deliberately not prescribed: the enum has no such value, and the record's F3 adds it to D2b's prescription when ADR-0073 M2 lands; the semantic entry's `replacement` names it under that condition. The spec tests assert all three channels and the absence of `'automation'` in both sentences; the metadata and protocol tests assert the three channels on their own envelopes.

**The `runAs` description change on `flow.zod.ts` — right.** The record itself names the description as the hazard ("prescribes `system` for user-less triggers, so an author who follows it opens an anonymous system-level door"). The diff keeps the existing text and appends the exception and the three serving channels; it cites an ADR id, not a tracker number. Text only; `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` (five tables) and `automation/flow.mdx` (two tables) are regenerated to the same sentence. The hook `runAs` text is untouched, which is right: a hook is not endpoint-triggered.

**The ADR anchor** (`scripts/adr-anchors/packages__spec__src__api__endpoint-publish-gate.ts.json`, new, naming ADR-0121 and ADR-0138 with the invariant) is PD #13's "one new JSON file per anchor", data for the existing `check:adr-anchors`, not a gate script; the record's "no new gate script" holds (no `scripts/check-*` is added).

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/23225-d2b-anonymous-elevated-flow-refused.md` grades `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor`; all three are published packages (no `private` flag) and each one's shipped code moves in the diff, so each owes the entry. It carries the BREAKING line (an accept-set narrowing shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention, the grade slices 1 and 2 used for their narrowings), the FROM → TO table per door, the one-line fix, and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The PR title `feat(spec)!:` matches the changeset's first line. **Clause-②: `yes (narrowing)` is right for this diff.** The value answers whether the card widens an accept set or the public surface: the diff adds eight exports to `@objectstack/spec/api` (`api-surface/api.json` +8), so `yes`; the arm says the diff also narrows a published accept set, so `(narrowing)`. The fleet's one reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) names `yes (narrowing)` as the combination for "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another: both facts are true and both are read". The triage's `no` and the claim's original line predate the measurement that the judge must be exported; the seat's in-place amendment of the claim (`6160651537`) and of PR body line 2 to `yes (narrowing)` makes the three carriers (claim, body, changeset) agree, and `check-changeset-no-major` admits either value because every moved package is `minor`. **The ADR-0087 `registered` entry exists in the diff and resolves.** The changeset carries one disposition marker (an HTML comment, spelled `adr-0087: registered api-endpoint-anonymous-elevated-flow-refused`), and the diff adds `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.api-endpoint-anonymous-elevated-flow-refused.ts` with exactly that `id`, in the directory the gate reads ids from (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, the semantic entries dir); the id is new in the diff, so the gate's "named id must be new" rule is met. `registered`, one new semantic entry, is the card row's disposition verbatim, and the entry's `reason` states why no conversion can choose a posture for the author. The head's `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` check-runs are `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag (the `os-dev-report` `6162772892`: nine deviations, one open question, two out-of-scope findings) and the PR's four acceptance notes, each answered or escalated:

- **Clause-② conflict (deviation 1; open question, options A/B).** Answered A by the seat, in place; judged right above. Nothing open.
- **File surface widened to `@objectstack/metadata` (deviation 2).** `MetadataManager.publishPackage` already calls `validateApiEndpointDeclarations`, so it is a measured endpoint publish door; leaving it out would have left the endpoint direction unenforced at a door the record's "every publish door that holds the pair" covers. The claim was widened at ACCEPT and the cross-lane declaration made on #6367. Inside the record.
- **`@objectstack/service-automation` unchanged (H2 falsified).** The claim and the ADR's Consumers line name that package for D2b; the dev measured that it judges no publish (it arms flows after the protocol publishes them), and said so in the report and the PR body rather than choosing silently. The record's enforcer is "the publish path", not a package name, and the stored-flow publish is the protocol's. Right; nothing the record requires is missing because of it.
- **New ADR anchor (deviation 3), section-5 pins on the existing double (deviation 4), body written at 71 of 125 gates (deviation 5), lock-queue re-runs (6), label and worktree notes (8, 9).** Noted; none moves the judgment. The report's final figures (125 derived, 125 run, 0 unmeasured) are the dev's; the check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts this record reads.
- **Merge commits without the trailer pair (deviation 7).** Outside this record's inputs; the PR lands as a squash whose subject is the title.
- **Restore doors not judged (out-of-scope finding 1; acceptance note 1).** `rollbackMetaItem` and `revertCommit`'s restore limb can re-activate a stored `runAs: 'system'` flow version while an anonymous endpoint names it, through the repository's synchronous `deriveRestoredBody`. The record decides "publish refuses ... in both directions" and its enforcement-map row reads "the publish path"; a restore is a third door the record did not name, and no cross-item refusal sits on it today. So the PR stays inside the decision and is not short of anything the record requires; whether D2b should reach the restore doors is an amendment question for the maintainer, and the ACCEPT says the seat carries it in its round report. Escalated, accepted as such.
- **Non-publish paths (out-of-scope finding 2; acceptance notes 2 and 3).** The endpoint matcher's load-time index holds no flows, a flow registered straight into the engine passes no publish, a cross-package pair is outside the stack door's scope, and there is no full runtime counterpart (`refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart` covers self-triggered types only, which the module header now states). Each is where the record's own words put it ("the publish path"); the module header's "every per-endpoint gate has a runtime counterpart" rewording keeps the header true. Acceptance notes, rightly.
- **The protocol reads endpoints without peeling (acceptance note 4).** A code-declared or package-published `api` row is flat (its body keys at the top level beside the bookkeeping), and the judge reads it correctly; a row registered directly through `metadata.register()` in the wrapped envelope shape is served by the matcher (which peels) but is not seen by the protocol's flow-direction read. The matcher's own header calls such a write "not a publish", so this is outside the record's path and rightly an acceptance note. Named for the seat: peeling at that read would bring the protocol's view of the declared endpoints to parity with the index the matcher serves from. Not a blocker.
- **The indirect path** (a guest-written row firing a record-change flow) is "recorded and not decided" in the record and is left alone by the diff, as the section (f) header and the semantic entry say.

Nothing the record's E2 row requires of D2b is missing: the refusal in both directions at every publish door the diff names, each refusal carrying the prescription, each pin with a negative control (the controls are in all three test files), the `registered` semantic entry, and the changeset carrying the row's disposition. The diff touches no governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; 16 paths, none in the register) and is under the 3,000-line class.

**Check-runs on the head, as found at the read (47 runs):** the five required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates` success; `TypeScript Type Check` success; `Build Core` success; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `Test Core` shards 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 of 6 success, shard `Test Core (3/6)` **in_progress at the read** (not polled). All other completed runs are `success` or roster `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, the dogfood shard matrix, Packed-tarball smoke, the second Auto Label and Check PR Size); no run has a failure conclusion. The landing waits on that shard's `success` as it waits on every check; this verdict does not substitute for it.
